unresolvedFindings.issue: Repair instruction from round 1 not carried out: final_article.md still has no standfirst and no authorPhoto. This is a verified site-builder defect, not a preference. tools/build/site.mjs:575 sets the page description as `meta.standfirst || meta.subtitle`, and site.mjs:756 renders the index-card excerpt the same way. With no standfirst, both the og:description and the article's card on the index page fall back to the eight-word subtitle "AI is about to make office politics expensive", where the already-published sibling site/content/the-great-corporate-unmasking-in-brief.md carries a full standfirst and authorPhoto: people/helena-carre.jpg. Intake G4 flagged the missing photo as a note; the standfirst consequence was flagged by me in round 1 and nothing in reports/integration.json acknowledges either (grep: no occurrence of 'standfirst' or 'authorPhoto').
unresolvedFindings.repair: Add two frontmatter keys to final_article.md, copied from the published sibling, changing nothing in the body: `standfirst: For decades, navigating office politics was a bulletproof career path. AI is about to turn it into a costly liability.` and `authorPhoto: people/helena-carre.jpg`. Then delete that same opening line from the body, because the published sibling keeps it in standfirst only and site.mjs:625 prints standfirst above the body, which would otherwise print it twice. Both strings are the author's own words already live on the site, so this adds nothing of yours. Record it in changes[].

unresolvedFindings.issue: Repair instruction from round 1 not carried out: the translation consequence is still unrecorded. reports/integration.json mentions Spanish exactly once, in passing, inside the longVersion change, and never states the requirement. The human choosing replace over duplicate needs this before they choose.

unresolvedFindings.issue: Advisory, no repair on your authority — for the human reviewer. Two substantive softenings in this run contradict wording the house has already published for this same article, so the site would end up stating two different strengths of the same claim on two live pages. (1) Section 1 bullet: the final says "An analyst with a few AI tools can run much of a consulting team's discovery phase themselves." The published site/content/the-great-corporate-unmasking-in-brief.md says "An analyst with a few AI tools can replace a consulting team's discovery phase in an afternoon." — the full, unhedged claim the Fact Checker rated UNVERIFIED with "Do not publish as established fact". (2) The final says "much harder to defend"; the published sibling carries "AI is making substance-free leadership impossible to defend." as a pull-quote. Both of this run's choices are the defensible ones and I am not asking for them to be reverted. The finding is that no agent in this run noticed the live page already ships what the Fact Checker said must not ship, which means the fact-check finding applies to a published page nobody has been asked to fix.
unresolvedFindings.repair: No change to final_article.md. Record for the human reviewer that the fact-check finding on the consulting claim also lands on the live in-brief page, and that whichever version survives, the two pages must not disagree about the strength of that claim.
